mission: Intuitive Machines IM-2, Nova-C lander 'Athena' (NASA CLPS)
landingSource: NASA: touched down 'at approximately 11:30 a.m. March 6' (CST)
contactEndSource: NASA: 'an early end of mission at 12:15 a.m. CST Friday'
attitude: on its side (NASA; LROC 1408: 'ended up on its side within a 20-meter diameter crater')
secondary: Wikipedia (citing CNN / Intuitive Machines): 'shadowed crater', solar arrays produced 'only about 100 watts'; secondary sources, used for comparison only
offsetNote: Distance between the two LROC coordinates; the target is given to 0.01° (±~150 m). NASA's release says 'more than 1,300 feet (400 meters)' in the text and 'about 820 feet' (~250 m) in an image caption.
craterNote: The 20 m crater is below the 120 m DEM resolution, so the LOLA horizon cannot contain it. 'craterFloorDarkIfDeeperThanM' is pure geometry: the floor centre sees no Sun if the crater is deeper than 10 m × tan(max Sun elevation + solar radius). The crater's depth is not published.
method: build.build_site: LOLA LDEM 120 m horizon (150 km rays), observer 2 m, JPL DE421 via Skyfield

target.name: Planned site (IM-2 target)
target.source: LROC image 1401 'IM-2 Landing Region' (26 Feb 2025): intended landing site (-84.78°, 29.13°E); given to 0.01° (about ±150 m)

actual.name: Actual site (Athena)
actual.source: LROC image 1408 'IM-2 Athena Seen Obliquely' (10 Mar 2025): on its side within a 20-meter diameter crater at 84.7906° S, 29.1957° E

nasaLongTerm.source: Mazarico, E., et al. (2011), Illumination conditions of the lunar polar regions using LOLA topography, Icarus 211, 1066-1081, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.10.030
